summary: This experimental document describes a BGP-based approach for building end-to-end paths that satisfy a specific intent, such as low latency, across a transport network that spans several domains. Service routes that need a particular intent can then be steered onto those paths.

eli5.summary: Different packages need different delivery: fast, cheap or safe. BGP CAR lets networks agree on routes labeled by what they are good for, even across many companies.

questions: what is bgp color aware routing
what is the local color mapping extended community
how does bgp car steer vpn traffic
subtitle: BGP routes that carry an intent, called a color, so one destination can have a separate path per intent across many domains.

tldr.problem: Operators want end-to-end paths with a specific intent, such as low delay, across a transport network made of several domains, without every node holding a forwarding entry for every egress PE and color.
tldr.mechanism: Two new BGP SAFIs, BGP CAR (83) and VPN CAR (84), distribute infrastructure routes keyed by prefix and color (Type-1) or by a per-intent prefix (Type-2). Each route resolves recursively over a color-aware path in the next domain, and service routes marked with a Color Extended Community are steered onto them automatically.
tldr.outcome: Hierarchical designs keep core routers from needing entries for every endpoint and color, and the same mechanism works for MPLS, SR-MPLS and SRv6. The document is Experimental.

today: RFC 9871 is an Experimental RFC, and no RFC obsoletes or updates it. It is not an Internet Standards Track specification.

sections.title: Intent, Color and the Big Picture
sections.content:
BGP Color-Aware Routing (CAR) builds end-to-end, intent-aware paths across a multi-domain provider transport network. An intent is a behavior that influences path selection, such as low cost, low delay, avoiding some resources, or a 5G network slice. A color is a non-zero 32-bit integer the operator associates with an intent, as in RFC 9256.

BGP CAR distributes different routes to the same destination, such as a PE router, for different colors. An egress PE colors its service routes with the BGP Color Extended Community, and the ingress PE automatically steers matching traffic onto the color-aware path (E, C) to that egress. The RFC states that BGP CAR keeps the flat routing model of BGP-IP and BGP-LU, so operation stays familiar.

If several mechanisms offer the same color-aware path, the default preference is IGP Flexible Algorithm, then SR Policy, then BGP CAR. Where none is available, local policy may fall back to a color-unaware path.
sections.eli5: A color is just a label for what you care about, like fast or safe. A package marked with a color gets sent along the road built for that color.

sections.title: Routes, Validation and Resolution
sections.content:
There are two NLRI types. Type-1 (E, C) is keyed by IP prefix and color, so one common address such as a loopback can have one route per intent. Type-2 (IP Prefix) is keyed by prefix alone, for cases where each intent has its own address block, such as per-intent SRv6 locators. Both SAFIs apply to AFI 1 and AFI 2, and the routes carry labels or SIDs in non-key TLVs.

A CAR path (E, C) via next hop N is valid only if a color-aware path (N, C) exists with the encapsulation available in the data plane; a path that is not valid MUST NOT be considered for best path selection. The route is resolved by default over (N, C), provided by IGP Flexible Algorithm, SR Policy or CAR itself, and domains resolve independently. Local policy can map a color to a different one, for example when a domain lacks a resource. The AIGP metric accumulates a value matching the intent, and BGP ADD-PATH SHOULD be enabled to signal multiple next hops through a transport route reflector.
sections.eli5: A road only counts if there is a matching road of the same color on the next stretch. Each stretch of road can be built by a different crew.

sections.title: NLRI, TLVs and the LCM Community
sections.content:
Every CAR NLRI starts with an NLRI Length, a Key Length and an NLRI Type, each one octet. The explicit key length lets route reflectors pass along unknown types without understanding them. Non-key TLVs have a one-octet type with a reserved bit, a Transitive bit and a 6-bit code, then a length and value. TLV type 1 is Label, type 2 is Label-Index and type 3 is SRv6 SID. On withdrawal the non-key TLVs MUST be omitted.

Different color domains can use different colors for the same intent. The new Local Color Mapping Extended Community (LCM-EC) carries the local color for a route when it crosses a domain boundary. The NLRI itself never changes. Where present, the LCM-EC color is used instead of the NLRI color for validation, resolution, AIGP and steering. LCM-EC is a Transitive Opaque Extended Community with Type 0x3 and Sub-Type 0x1b.

Errors follow RFC 7606: malformed NLRIs that can be skipped are treated as withdrawn, and otherwise the router disables the AFI/SAFI or resets the session.
sections.eli5: Each route is a small packed message with a built-in ruler saying how long each part is, so even routers that do not know the newest kind can pass it along safely.

sections.title: Scaling with Hierarchy
sections.content:
The scaling goals are that no intermediate node should need a data plane sized to colors times PEs, and no node should install a route to (E, C) unless it installs a colored service route to E. In the reference topology, a flat design works but core border routers must hold entries for every egress and color. The RFC gives an example of 300k endpoints and 5 colors, which makes 1.5M entries, more than a 1M MPLS data plane.

Hierarchical designs fix that: core routers only need routes to the egress border routers. The ingress border router either sets itself as next hop, which hides the hierarchy from the ingress PE, or leaves the next hop unchanged, which makes the ingress PE push more labels. Filtering by color, RT Constrain and on-demand route installation can also limit what each node learns. Anycast SIDs and failure handling within a domain help convergence.
sections.eli5: If every town on the highway had to know every address in the country, the signs would not fit. Instead, the middle towns just know the way to the big exits.

sections.title: SRv6, VPNs and Security
sections.content:
For SRv6, an egress PE can allocate its service SID from a routed, intent-aware locator, and the Type-2 IP Prefix route distributes those locators across domains. A non-routed service SID is advertised with a Color-EC and steered over Type-1 routes. For VPNs, VPN CAR (SAFI 84) adds a Route Distinguisher to the NLRI key so overlapping customer address spaces stay separate.

The document's security text says it adds no change to BGP's inherent issues, but that the new SAFI is a new way to divert traffic. BGP sessions SHOULD be protected with the TCP Authentication Option and GTSM, and the SAFI should be configured explicitly with route policy filters. Using a separate SAFI keeps infrastructure routes apart from service routes. LCM-EC and Color-EC MUST NOT be filtered, or the intent is lost. IANA assigned SAFI values 83 and 84, created registries for NLRI types and TLV types, and assigned sub-type 0x1b.
sections.eli5: The same color idea works for IPv6 addresses and for private company networks. Because this is a new lane of BGP, operators must lock it down carefully so nobody can send traffic the wrong way.
